title: Older adult scam prevention
audience: Older adults and trusted community supporters
objectives: Identify pressure and impersonation without relying on caller ID or a familiar voice.
Demonstrate an independent callback using a fictional request.
Choose the affected bank or service as an immediate response destination after a suspected scam.

outline.title: Welcome and choice
outline.activity: Explain scope, privacy, and the option to pass. Ask participants to name a task they want more confidence doing without describing past losses.
outline.prompt: What would make this session comfortable for you?

outline.title: Recognize pressure
outline.activity: Read a fictional message claiming a bank needs a transfer. Identify the requested decision rather than judging the participant.
outline.prompt: What is being requested, and what could wait?

outline.title: Phone, message, and AI impersonation
outline.activity: Discuss why an official-looking number or familiar-sounding voice does not establish identity. Do not play cloned voices or stage a surprise call.
outline.prompt: What can you check independently of what you hear?

outline.title: Practice verification
outline.activity: On paper, work through a fictional family money request. Choose a known callback route and a second contact; no actual numbers or transfers.
outline.prompt: If the first trusted person cannot answer, what is your next safe step?

outline.title: Respond without further loss
outline.activity: Use the immediate-action handout to choose bank, account, or device help for three fictional situations.
outline.prompt: Which service can act on the affected payment or account?

outline.title: Takeaway and feedback
outline.activity: Invite each participant to explain one step in their own words. Collect optional feedback about clarity, not personal incidents.
outline.prompt: What will you practice next, and what support would help?

takeaways: An independent callback is a normal safety step, not an accusation.
No one needs to share passwords with a helper.
Act promptly after suspected fraud without promises of recovery.

title: Parent and family digital safety
audience: Parents, guardians, caregivers, and family-serving organizations
objectives: Identify privacy, contact, and purchase settings to review together.
Explain an independent family verification step and appropriate reporting route.

outline.title: Set a supportive tone
outline.activity: Explain that families have different needs and may pass. Avoid comparing parenting decisions.
outline.prompt: What would help a child feel able to ask for help?

outline.title: Age-appropriate privacy
outline.activity: Compare a fictional young child profile with a fictional teen profile. Choose which details should remain private without viewing real accounts.
outline.prompt: How would your explanation change with the child’s understanding?

outline.title: Gaming and messaging
outline.activity: Discuss an invented prize message in plain text. Do not create a functioning link or ask participants to simulate coercion.
outline.prompt: What access or information does the request ask for?

outline.title: AI and family verification
outline.activity: Explain that synthetic media cannot prove identity. Choose a known callback route for an imagined family request.
outline.prompt: How can adults model pausing rather than demanding instant decisions?

outline.title: Practice a supportive response
outline.activity: In pairs or individually, complete the parent conversation guide. Practice the adult’s calm response to a child asking for help, with no exploitation role-play.
outline.prompt: What could you say before asking detailed questions?

outline.title: Reporting and next steps
outline.activity: Review platform reporting, trusted adults, and NCMEC resources. Each participant chooses one household setting or conversation to revisit.
outline.prompt: Who can help when an issue is beyond a household rule?

takeaways: Settings support ongoing conversations; they do not replace them.
Help comes before blame or a discussion of broken rules.
Never forward intimate images to seek advice.

title: Teen digital safety
audience: Teenagers, with a prepared adult facilitator and host safeguarding contact
objectives: Identify an account or social pressure request that deserves a pause.
Explain why images, voices, and account names do not by themselves prove identity.
Find a trusted adult and appropriate reporting support without needing to disclose personal harm.

outline.title: Choice and boundaries
outline.activity: Explain privacy, the right to pass, and where to seek private help. Do not promise confidentiality that conflicts with safeguarding responsibilities.
outline.prompt: What makes asking for help easier?

outline.title: Identity and privacy
outline.activity: Use a fictional profile and ask what strangers could learn. Never open students’ accounts or ask for identifying information.
outline.prompt: Which details would you choose not to share publicly?

outline.title: Scams and AI-generated content
outline.activity: Use a benign text example asking for a game-account code. Discuss social pressure and independent checking; no deepfake generation or exploitation scenarios.
outline.prompt: What action matters more than whether a message looks convincing?

outline.title: Boundaries and safe help-seeking
outline.activity: Give a short non-graphic explanation of sextortion as threats involving intimate images. State that it is not the person’s fault, that payment/more images are not a safe solution, and point to trusted adults and NCMEC. No role-play, images, or disclosure prompts.
outline.prompt: Which adult or support route could someone approach without explaining it to the group?

outline.title: Practice and takeaways
outline.activity: Use the teen checklist with fictional account settings. Invite a voluntary explanation of one safety choice. Offer private written questions without names.
outline.prompt: What would you tell a friend who needs help?

extension: Optional 15 minutes: repeat the benign account-code exercise using a different fictional request, allow a break, and answer general questions. Do not extend the sensitive-content discussion through personal examples.
takeaways: You can leave a conversation even if someone pressures you.
A trusted adult can help with reporting and account recovery.
Do not pay blackmail demands or forward intimate images; seek support.
